subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Reed <t.reed@finsecure.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Thomas — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of your requirements:
- Strict data isolation: customer-managed network boundaries and no egress of raw customer input outside your environment.
- KMS/HSM support and BYOK for encryption keys.
- Audit logs retained for 1 year; ability to export logs to your SIEM.
- SOC2 + penetration testing evidence for procurement.

Platform fit guidance (high level):
- Hosted API: great for fast prototyping, but not suitable for your isolation needs — data passes through our hosted control plane and multitenant network.
- Dedicated capacity: dedicated GPU pools and isolated compute, with strong tenant separation. However, control plane and some orchestration services remain hosted; useful when you need hardware isolation and better performance guarantees but still accept a Redwood-managed control plane.
- Private VPC / On-prem: customer-managed VPC or on-prem deployment gives you the strongest network and data isolation guarantees (no outbound data by default, your own KMS/HSM, and full control over egress). This is the model most customers choose when procurement/legal require no external control-plane data flow.

Questions from the call I noted:
1) Do your legal/compliance teams require a deployed control plane inside your network (yes/no)?
2) Are there any regulatory constraints around model weights staying inside the customer environment?

Proposed next steps:
- I will send a short architecture note contrasting Dedicated vs Private VPC and specifically call out where logs, keys, and model telemetry live (attached).
- If Private is the likely path, we can schedule a 1-hour workshop with Solutions Architecture (Vivek) and your infra/security team to map gaps and confirm SOW/OPS.
- I'll also attach our latest SOC2 report and a sample audit log export spec for your SIEM team.

Attached: redwood-vpc-arch.pdf, soc2-report-2026.pdf

If that aligns, can you pls confirm whether legal needs the control plane in-network and suggest 2 slots next week for the workshop?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Looping in with a short note for the workshop prep. I can cover the control-plane separation options and the operational requirements for a Private VPC deployment. Key points to highlight for FinSecure:

- Private VPC (managed control plane variant): customer controls network (VPC peering or private link), we deploy a control plane component into the customer's VPC or provide a customer-hosted control-plane bundle. No customer inputs/outputs are persisted in our hosted systems by default.
- On-prem variant: full air-gapped option; we ship an on-prem package and coordinate updates; ideal when legal requires zero external control-plane contact.
- Dedicated capacity: isolated compute but retains Redwood-managed control-plane telemetry for scheduling and runtime optimizations. We can limit telemetric data and provide contractual assurances, but some orchestration metadata remains with Redwood.

For pricing: Private VPC carries an Ops/setup surcharge and a higher base licensing fee vs Dedicated (rough ballpark: +20-50% depending on support/SLA). We should surface that to procurement early.

I'll be available for the workshop on Tue 12/8 10-11am PT or Wed 12/9 2-3pm PT.

-Vivek
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Thomas Reed <t.reed@finsecure.com>

Date: 2026-12-02T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Marissa — thanks. Legal confirms they want the control plane resident in our VPC (managed by us or deployed as customer-hosted). A couple more items they asked to confirm ahead of the workshop:

1) KMS/HSM: can we BYOK and integrate with our HSM provider (Thales) so keys never leave our environment?
2) Audit logs: can we receive a continuous export (syslog/JSON) to our Splunk instance and confirm retention settings are configurable (we need 12 months)?
3) Model telemetry: we need a clear list of what telemetry Redwood requires if any — distinguish between operational telemetry (CPU/memory/queue lengths) and behavioral telemetry (examples, prompts).

If we can get answers to 1-3 and a rough SOW outline and pricing delta prior to the workshop that would help legal/procurement. We can do Tue 12/8 10am PT for the workshop — that works for the infra/security team.

Thanks,
Thomas Reed
Head of Cloud Security | FinSecure
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Reed <t.reed@finsecure.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T10:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Thomas — great, thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers ahead of the workshop and what we'll bring:

1) KMS/HSM / BYOK: yes — Private VPC and on-prem both support BYOK. We have integrations for common HSM providers (Thales, AWS CloudHSM). Keys remain in your KMS/HSM; we never persist plaintext keys in the Redwood control plane. We'll include an integration checklist for Thales in the workshop pack.

2) Audit logs: we can stream audit and access logs to your Splunk via secure syslog or S3 export. Retention can be configured on your side (we will provide export formats and a sample retention policy).

3) Model telemetry: for Private VPC we can disable behavioral telemetry collection by default. Operational telemetry required for runtime stability (CPU, memory, KV cache metrics, and throughput) can be exported to your monitoring if desired; we'll provide an explicit telemetry matrix in the workshop doc.

What we'll deliver before the workshop (by EOD Mon 12/6):
- Detailed architecture note highlighting control-plane placement options and egress controls (attached earlier).
- Integration checklist for BYOK/HSM (Thales) and log export spec.
- Ballpark SOW/pricing delta worksheet for Dedicated vs Private (range and drivers).

Confirmed workshop: Tue 12/8 at 10:00am PT — Vivek will lead the architecture portion; Rishi will be on pricing and escalation terms.

If legal wants, we can also provide a redlineable appendix that enumerates telemetry commitments (what we collect, what we do not).

See you on 12/8 — I'll send calendar invites and the workshop deck.

Best,
Marissa Cole
